issue.title: [Project]: FlightBench
issue.body:
### GitHub repository (项目仓库地址)

https://github.com/AlperKartkaya/FlightBench

### What does it do? (项目核心用途)

FlightBench is a fixed-wing plane landing simulator and benchmark for decision models, LLMs, and classical controllers. You can run the simulator, land the plane, and compete with Jev. Jev lands the aircraft, receiving the state of the plane and four Choice decisions, and returning (the probability distributions of) the actuator commands. The commands are applied to the plane with JSBSim.

### Jev Primitives used (使用的 Jev 核心原语)

⚡ Choice (离散动作/分支多选一 · N-Pick-1)

### Primary Category (建议主分类)

High-Frequency & Simulation (高频仿真与游戏)

### Project Tags (项目场景标签，建议选 1~3 个)

games-simulation (游戏与仿真 / Games & Simulation)

### Where does Jev make a decision? (Jev 在哪里做决策 / 源码证据)

Jev receives the state of the aircraft and four Choice questions for aircraft control (namely: aileron, elevator, rudder, and throttle), returning (the probability distributions of) the actuator commands.

- What Jev Sees and What It Delivers: https://github.com/AlperKartkaya/FlightBench#what-jev-sees
- Method: https://github.com/AlperKartkaya/FlightBench#how-is-jevs-api-used
- Recording of Jev's Flight: https://alperkartkaya.github.io/FlightBench/jev-flight/

### Submission Checklist (收录合规确认)

- [x] 该仓库是公开可访问的真实开源项目（非私有、非空壳/占位项目）
- [x] 仓库根目录或代码中包含声明清晰的开源协议（如 MIT、Apache-2.0、GPL 等）
- [x] 我已知晓项目将由自动化流水线进行固定版本源码核查与自动归档

FlightBench

Can you land a plane better than Jev?
FlightBench is a landing simulator and benchmark for decision models, LLMs, and classical controllers.
Try landing it yourself first, and compete with Jev, Codex, or your friends!

## Jev lands the plane! [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction) is [TypeSafe](https://www.typesafe.ai)'s System One decision model. Given a state and typed questions, it returns structured choices and probabilities. Here, the right panel shows the state sent to Jev and the four actuator commands that Jev chose. **[Watch the full flight!](https://alperkartkaya.github.io/FlightBench/jev-flight/)** ## Can you beat my landing? **[Watch my flight!](https://alperkartkaya.github.io/FlightBench/human-flight/)** My record is **70.1/100**. Try the same setup and beat my score, then [send me your run or recording](mailto:alperkartkaya@gmail.com)! You can also [watch the baseline controller](https://alperkartkaya.github.io/FlightBench/baseline-flight/). ## Quick take-off ### Requirements - Python 3.11–3.13 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download) 20.19+ (20.x) or 22.12+, with npm ```sh uv sync uv run uvicorn flightbench.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 # In another terminal: cd frontend && npm ci && npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 ``` Open , choose a controller, and select **Start flight**. Human-pilot and baseline modes require neither an API key nor a Codex account. For Jev, run `uv sync --extra jev` and set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`. For Codex, run `uv sync --extra codex`, install the Codex CLI, then authenticate with `codex login` and check `codex login status`; this connection uses a [ChatGPT plan (free, plus, or pro) with Codex CLI access](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing), not an API key. See [llm-openai-via-codex](https://github.com/simonw/llm-openai-via-codex). ## Benchmark results and estimated API cost Where Jev landed successfully in realtime at an effective rate of about 2.4 calls per second, no Codex model managed to land successfully even with 2 Hz lockstep. Jev's performance is **not a 5-star one**, it performed with a 14% successful landing, 74% runway excursion, 9% nose-first contact (crash), and 2% timeout rate. The baseline controller landed with a score of **69.9/100**, a little below [my personal best](https://alperkartkaya.github.io/FlightBench/human-flight/)! | Controller | Score and result | Sim time and wall time (s) | Calls | Mean latency per call (s) | Latency vs Jev | Input / output tokens | Est. API cost | Cost vs Jev | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | **Jev · TypeSafe API** | **56 · landed** | 71 / 71 (realtime) | 168 (~2.4 Hz) | **0.33** | **1.0×** | ~291k / — | **$0.0122** | **1.0×** | | GPT-6 Luna (low) · Codex | 0 · nose-first contact | 39 / 202 (lockstep) | 79 (~0.4 Hz) | 2.53 | 7.7× | 78k / 5k | ≈$0.0153† | ≈1.3×† | | GPT-6 Sol (low) · Codex | 49 · runway excursion | 61 / 463 (lockstep) | 122 (~0.3 Hz) | 3.77 | 11.5× | 121k / 11k | $0.3521 | ≈29× | | GPT-6 Astra (low) · Codex | 49 · runway excursion | 61 / 558 (lockstep) | 123 (~0.2 Hz) | 4.50 | 13.8× | 122k / 11k | $1.758 | ≈143× | † Luna's observed 79-call cost is $0.01009. In the table, Luna's run is scaled to **120 calls** to roughly match the number of steps in the other models' runs. > While **Realtime** means simulation time equals wall clock time, **Lockstep** means the simulation is paused for each step to let the model respond. Hence, simulation and wall time can differ in lockstep. ## Landing score vs. estimated API cost ![Performance on FlightBench: best landing score versus estimated API cost](docs/benchmark-cost-performance.svg) **Estimate basis:** Jev's input-token estimate uses a four-characters-per-token proxy on the selected run's logged JSON, priced at [TypeSafe's $0.042/1M rate](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev). Codex token usage is based on the selected session logs, priced at [OpenAI Standard short-context rates](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing): Luna $0.10/$0.50, Sol $2/$10, Astra $10/$50 per million input/output tokens. Cached/cache-write tokens were zero, and output includes reasoning. The Codex runs used a **Codex subscription**, not pay-as-you-go API keys. The reported costs are **API-key equivalents**, not actual Codex charges. See [llm-openai-via-codex](https://github.com/simonw/llm-openai-via-codex). Successful landing threshold is a score of 50, and only Jev managed to surpass it. Also, Jev's flight was run in realtime, whereas for Codex, the UI uses lockstep so physics waits for each model response. ## How is Jev's API used? ![How Jev steers FlightBench: an aircraft-state snapshot leads to four textual Choice answers, fixed commands, and a JSBSim physics step](docs/jev-control-loop.svg) *Illustrative choices from the mock request and response below.* ### What Jev sees The following **mock request** shows the structure of the state and questions sent to Jev. ```json { "model": "jev-1.13.0", "state": { "flight": {"airspeed_mps": 30.1, "vertical_speed_mps": -2.0, "roll_deg": 1.5, "pitch_deg": 2.8}, "runway": {"altitude_agl_m": 45, "centerline_offset_m": 3.0, "heading_error_deg": 1.5, "glideslope_error_deg": 0.2}, "current_controls": {"aileron": -0.15, "elevator": 0.17, "rudder": 0.09, "throttle": 0.5}, "time_s": 35, "motion": {"cross_track_rate_mps": 0.6}, "status": {"on_ground": false}, "phase": "APPROACH" }, "questions": { "aileron": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Choose an absolute aileron correction; arrest bank, then sideways motion, then offset.", "criteria": { "0": "Strong left roll", "1": "Moderate left roll", "2": "Gentle left roll", "3": "Maintain a small bank", "4": "Gentle right roll", "5": "Moderate right roll", "6": "Strong right roll" } }, "elevator": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Choose an absolute elevator correction for the approach glidepath.", "criteria": { "0": "Emergency nose-up", "1": "Strong nose-up", "2": "Firm nose-up", "3": "Nose-up recovery", "4": "Nose-up support", "5": "Moderate nose-up support", "6": "Mild nose-up support", "7": "Normal descent", "8": "Moderate nose-down", "9": "Strong nose-down" } }, "rudder": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Choose an absolute rudder correction for heading and yaw.", "criteria": { "0": "Strong yaw right", "1": "Moderate yaw right", "2": "Gentle yaw right", "3": "Trim yaw", "4": "Gentle yaw left", "5": "Moderate yaw left", "6": "Strong yaw left" } }, "throttle": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Choose absolute throttle for airspeed and flight phase.", "criteria": { "0": "Idle", "1": "Reduced flare power", "2": "Slightly reduced approach power", "3": "Normal approach power", "4": "Increased approach power", "5": "High approach power", "6": "Full power" } } } } ``` ### What Jev delivers The following **mock response** shows the selected labels and the *per actuator* probability distributions, along with the confidence. ```json { "model": "jev-1.13.0", "answers": { "aileron": { "type": "choice", "choice": "2", "confidence": 0.64, "probabilities": {"0": 0.02, "1": 0.06, "2": 0.70, "3": 0.16, "4": 0.04, "5": 0.01, "6": 0.01} }, "elevator": { "type": "choice", "choice": "7", "confidence": 0.51, "probabilities": {"0": 0, "1": 0, "2": 0, "3": 0.01, "4": 0.02, "5": 0.05, "6": 0.17, "7": 0.65, "8": 0.08, "9": 0.02} }, "rudder": { "type": "choice", "choice": "4", "confidence": 0.58, "probabilities": {"0": 0.01, "1": 0.02, "2": 0.06, "3": 0.16, "4": 0.65, "5": 0.08, "6": 0.02} }, "throttle": { "type": "choice", "choice": "3", "confidence": 0.68, "probabilities": {"0": 0, "1": 0.01, "2": 0.09, "3": 0.72, "4": 0.12, "5": 0.04, "6": 0.02} } } } ``` ## A few remarks - **Jev's control loop.** FlightBench sends Jev a snapshot of the aircraft, runway, current controls, motion, and flight phase. Each request asks Jev to choose an aileron, elevator, rudder, and throttle correction. Jev returns a selected label and a separate probability distribution for each actuator. The controller maps those labels to fixed absolute commands. JSBSim computes the resulting flight based on these commands and the aircraft's state. - **Codex and realtime.** Codex models ran in **2 Hz lockstep**: physics waited for each answer, so slow responses did not directly cause those failed landings. Sol and Astra ended in runway excursions in all five runs; Luna had two nose-first contacts and three crashes. Their mean decision latencies of 2.53–4.50 seconds are far beyond the 0.5-second interval needed for 2 Hz realtime control. This reveals one of the most important advantages of decision models like Jev over general purpose LLMs. - **Runway excursions.** A runway excursion is still a failed landing, but it is useful in means of showing an improvement over crash scenerios: in a runway excursion, the aircraft reaches touchdown before leaving the runway bounds. In the further studies and revisions, the controller can be improved to be less prone to runway excursions; as it showed up to be the biggest challenge for the LLMs. - **Controller design.** During the development process, I found it useful to use acceptance thresholds on the probabilities of the selected choices to foster robustness. As the simulation was very prone to lose the stability, I also needed to tune the sensitivity of the choices Jev returned. It was difficult to initialize a balanced delta value, which was used to increase or decrease each of the four actuators, according to Jev's decisions. These were the challenges until I introduced fixed choices of values, which had a textual correspondence, hence making it easier for Jev to work with the controller. - **Decision rate.** In terms of the practical concerns, besides the obvious trade-off between the request rate and the API-cost, it is important to note that there is an upper limit on the effective request rate, which was 2.4 calls per second during my evaluation. To increase this effective request rate of 2.4 Hz, you can consider decreasing the simulation speed. I managed to increase it up to 10 Hz, halving the simulation speed twice. Note that this is currently not supported in the UI. ## Contributing Contributions of any size are welcome: report a bug, share a flight recording, suggest a controller, improve the docs, or send a pull request. ## License and credits FlightBench is [MIT licensed](LICENSE). Aircraft visual: [Small Airplane](https://poly.pizza/m/7cvx6ex-xfL) by Vojtěch Balák · [CC BY 3.0](frontend/public/models/LICENSE.md). Built with [JSBSim](https://jsbsim-team.github.io/jsbsim/python/FGFDMExec.html), [Gymnasium](https://gymnasium.farama.org/api/env/), [Three.js](https://threejs.org/), [TypeSafe Jev](https://typesafe.ai/), [llm-openai-via-codex](https://github.com/simonw/llm-openai-via-codex), and *passion*.
